texts: Patients with extensive collaterals may have minimal symptoms: C.
In pulmonary atresia with VSD, all the lung blood flow comes through the MAPCAs; when they are many and large, saturations are good and the child may even develop heart failure from too much flow.
With few or narrowed collaterals the infant is cyanotic, but there are no cyanotic spells from infundibular spasm, as the right ventricle has no outlet to the lungs.
The VSD is large and unrestrictive, and not all patients are symptomatic at birth.
In the picture, the baby with the crowded treasure map stays pink and calm, while the one with few paths turns blue.
Memory hook: a crowded treasure map, a pink baby.
